 1                       CHAIRMAN NIEH: Okay, good afternoon, everyone, I’ll call

 2   this meeting to order.

 3                       Appreciate the accommodation of the start time of 1:30

 4   instead of 1:00.

 5                       So, today we’re bringing together the Nuclear Regulatory

 6   Commission and the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.

 7                       And on behalf of the NRC, it’s my pleasure to welcome

 8   Chairman Swett and her fellow FERC Commissioners to NRC headquarters.

 9                       Thanks for making the trip up here, really appreciate that.

10                       This meeting marks 20 years since the first meeting

11   between our Commissions.

12                       That meeting grew out of the 2003 Northeast -- North

13   American Blackout event, which during that event, nine U.S. reactors tripped

14   offline, and that event highlighted the importance of grid reliability and nuclear

15   safety.

16                       Since then, the NRC and the FERC staff have been working

17   together under a Memo of Agreement to ensure that our work activities are

18   well coordinated.

19                       This meeting also comes at a really important time for

20   America’s energy system.

21                       The North American Electric Reliability Corporation’s latest

22   long-term assessment warns that America’s surging energy demand is
                                                                                     4

 1   outpacing new generation and transmission and presenting increased risk to

 2   America’s grid system.

 3                     The FERC’s assessment report also recognizes that

 4   nuclear is a non-variable source of dependable capacity to America’s grid.

 5                     And it also flanks the consequence that, if nuclear plants

 6   retire early before generation is ready, that could really impact our energy

 7   capacity in the United States.

 8                     This is the reason why many of NRC stakeholders see

 9   nuclear, which now generates about 19 percent of America’s electricity, as

10   essential to our energy security.

11                     This is also why the NRC is undergoing the most

12   comprehensive period of reform in over 50 years.

13                     President Trump and Congress have called on the NRC to

14   enable and accelerate the safe and secure deployment of new nuclear and

15   expand existing capacity.

16                     Some new nuclear will be provided directly to dedicated

17   customers, others will be powered to the grid, and that’s where FERC comes

18   in.

19                     FERC will help ensure that that power to the grid is delivered

20   reliably, securely, and cost effectively to the American consumer.

21                     So, I’m really looking forward to the presentations from the

22   FERC and NRC staff today.

23                     And with that, I’d like to turn it over to Chairman Laura Swett

24   from FERC for opening remarks.
